posts.cooked:
So I lost my ENTIRE team except a 4-health Nightmist in round 4ish to an Entomb. thanks to Akash dropping every freaking limb in the game.  I then spent the next hour slowly tanking my way back up to full health with NightMist while the environment went to town on the Limbs.  Thanks to the Ensnaring Brambles, I had NightMist's entire deck in her hand and was pitching 4-star cards constantly and cycling Mistbinds to keep her health up until the Brambles were eliminated and it was safe to start sniping.  Amulet of the Elder Gods is a lifesaver when you're drawing 12+ cards a turn with no drawback.  There were a couple of dicy moments where I had to let Akash play a card or two and she pretty much wiped the board each time, but we got there!

posts.name: Kratos13
posts.cooked:
Whew got the mint!

Lucky start with Inspiring Presence, Electrical Storm, Submachine Gun so lots of area damage right away.  Too afraid to get Unitys Bots out without any Stealth protection.  Got Amulet right away, but lost all equipment to Rejuvenating Entropy and didn't get another one til way later.  Luckily, had a second Submachine Gun to replace the first and got Hairtrigger Reflexes.  Tempest eventually gets Hailstorm. So Expat and Tempest were doing great area damage on their own and got her to about 118 pretty quickly.  

Unlucky break: double Primeval Eruption so there were 3 Brambles, 2 Rockslides, 2 Phalanges and 2 Carapaces out.  Brambles always seemed to target Nightmist.  Kinda lucky actually; without the Necklace, could hunt for cards with Enlightment or Investigation without hurting herself.  Cleared the Rockslides and eventually the other limbs the following round.

Another unlucky break: Earth's Sacrifice takes out Inspring Presence, Hairtrigger Reflexes, Electrical Storm, Hailstorm. But Akash is down to around 60 HP.  I start playing Tempest defensively and do Cleansing Downpour.  But for the others I go for broke with all the Thokks, Backfisted Strikes, Shotgun, Chain Lightning.  I finally get 2 Raptors but they die to New Jersey Devil right after. Platform and Cryo do come out and help a little and a few Brainstorms.

Final blow: Shotgun kills Rockslide ->kills Akash.

She flipped once in the middle of the game and then one more time just before she died.

Final Wasteland did not appear til late and no cards were lost to the Wasteland.

With Cleansing Downpour, everyone was at approx 10 HP.

I have mixed feelings about Random Start.  I did play duplicate bridge in my day, so I actually like everyone having the same initial conditions.  I feel there is a better common talking point and also a little more meaningful to me if someone else gets a mint, but I lose: since it was the same seed, I'd more feel like I could've made better choices vs. blame the loss on bad card shuffle and draw.

However, with enough strong familiarly with all decks, I believe good players can also play more robustly than others, i.e. try to anticipate certain bad case scenarios and make choices to accomodate; be flexible and adapt, etc.  Hence, Random Start can still be a good way to measure players.  Although extreme bad luck will still feel disappointing.

Overall, enjoying the One-Shots a lot!

posts.name: Kerredai
posts.cooked:
Mint, by the skin of my teeth -- a thoroughly enjoyable game, all around. 

Akash'Bhuta digs through her deck so fast in the Final Wasteland that I saw numerous 'reset' cards -- Earth's Sacrifice and Rejuvenating Entropy came out on a regular basis, making it difficult to get sufficiently set up to deal with the many limbs. I kept melting down Equipment with Unity's Bot-Hack -- knowing that it wouldn't last anyway -- but so many creatures in the Final Wasteland seem to pick on the lowest target; it was difficult to keep any bots in play for long.

The big break was getting a second Reclaim from the Deep to go with the one I'd been hoarding since the opening hand -- allowing Tempest to Reclaim his other Reclaim every turn and provide infinite cycling for cards like Take Down, Heroic Interception and Mistbind. This would have been a much cleaner game if I hadn't been a fool and shuffled Mistbind back into Nightmist's deck with e.g. Mist-Fueled Recovery. Twice. Man, you never really appreciate that Rewind button until it gets taken away...

I did lose Legacy, and everyone else was in single digits, but he died a hero -- specifically, Heroically Intercepting the damage from a desperate Oblivion play which provided enough damage to close out the game before Entomb killed most of the party.

posts.name: ClericalError
posts.cooked:
Mint!

I have to say, Akash'Bhuta is one of my favorite enemies to go against when I'm playing solo because the length of the game is always going to be a longer one than that of Baron Blade or his squishier counterparts, so I've had a lot of experience against this particular scenario. Not to mention two of my favorite characters are Legacy and Unity. :)

The way I won was actual mostly due to my re-use of Take-Down and the many "Reclaim from the Deep" cards I got. I would play Take-Down, kill a bunch of environment targets (so Akash'Bhuta wouldn't get the play advantage), let StealthBot tank enough hits to get to 1 hp so the Phallanges would be preventing no damage and my RaptorBots were happy to eat any limbs that came out of the works :)

I didn't actually realise the wording on the Advanced Akash'Bhuta until this game. The advanced text doesn't hit the bots! Unity so OP in the right circumstances.

posts.name: bessyrocks12

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
Mint, with an opening draw that I can't tell if it was lucky or unlucky. Before I had any kind of ongoing destruction in hand, Akash's first three cards were all Entomb. On the one hand, this meant everyone taking 15 HP of damage by the end of the second round (thanks, environment target). On the other, it meant I didn't have to worry about Entomb popping up unexpectedly for the rest of the game. No Primeval Eruptions, and the ongoing and equipment wipes came out early enough that I didn't have much on the field anyway, so it didn't wreck me.

Con's bunker came out the same round Legacy picked up a Take Down, so I was able to start getting the card draw up and running quick. Expatriette spent the whole time plugging away with her shotgun, while Unity had to wait a couple rounds to get bots out because of the Entombs (even though she started with equipment and Swiftbot in-hand; a bit frustrating, but necessary), but by the time she was ready to roll, boy did she roll with Platform, Bee and Raptor Bots doing their jobs. Nightmist dutifully tossed damage back at Akash and her limbs, and Mistbound her three times, which let me keep drawing from the Bunker. Tempest got his Localized Hurricane out early and ended up with damn near all his cards in hand, Cleansing Downpour showing up just in the nick of time. He was invaluable in cleaning up the Environment targets, especially after the first three kept drawing from the bunker, while Unity played clean-up duty and finished her off with a Shockwave powered by Swift, Stealth and Champion Bots.

Everyone survived, and the Environment only claimed one Rockslide.

http://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198100350547/screenshot/364030656452239854

Edit: Forgot to add, but this was my first time ever playing Advanced mode.

posts.name: Nielzabub
posts.cooked: I have double mint for this challenge now. Things looked bad when entomb got played on the environment turn and then on her turn an eruption got us two rockslides, but both got taken out. Unity managed to get all three raptor bots out with a champion bot and an inspiring presence doing well over thirty damage to Akash on that turn. It was hard to get going, but once we had all our stuff together, the tide turned.

posts.name: NinjaMonkey
posts.cooked:
Mint.

It was the perfect opening draw for all heroes except maybe Unity. Legacy started with a Bolster Allies, Take Down and Heroic Interception. Tempest started with Reclaim from the Deep. Nightmist started with Mistbound and Astral Premonition (think that's right, lets her discard a card to control the villain deck). Expat started with Assault Rifle, Hair Trigger Reflexes, and 2 RPG Launchers.

I foolishly gave Akash'bhuta a free pass on the first round to get a little setup before I started whittling her down. Paid for it with an out of turn Entomb, followed by back to back Primeval Eruptions. Ouch.

Between Nightmist, Legacy, and Tempest who drew a second Reclaim from the Deep on round 3, Akash got to play exactly 1 additional card. That one additional card was the vines limb (forget the name) which was put there by Nightmist and only damaged a single hero before it was taken down.

The environment was a factor as well. The Ancient Library was the first card out and I used it to fill my hands while drawing out beasts, and the Unforgiving Wasteland. The beasts took down the 7 or so limbs Akash had drawn with those two earlier Primeval Eruptions.

By the end of the game, Unity had out almost all the bots and was slamming Akash for 30+ points a round.

I actually felt sorry for Akash. Maybe she can keep Baron Blade company in the perenial loser's lounge.
